description: Words and phrases that make a verdict, score, ranking, approval or recommendation. Marked by plain code on the model's answer and on the text a tool returns outside quoted-source fields (never by another model). Whole words, case-insensitive. Phrases in allowPhrases are masked first. Official government ranks may be quoted with source, edition and level (decision 0054), so 'rank', 'decile' and 'index' are not listed; 'best' and 'worst' still are, because a quoted rank is not a verdict.
sources: AGENTS.md rule 4: never says a home is verified, safe or approved; AI never calculates numbers
Decision 0004: the chat never says a home is safe or verified
Decision 0054: we never make a score, a total or a ranking of our own; quoting an official rank is allowed
WCHAT-78: says the area is verified or approved (verified, approved)
WCHAT-79: calls the area the best (best)
WCHAT-80: a recommendation, 'you should buy here' (recommend, you should)
WCHAT-68: a score such as '4 out of 10', stopped even when its numbers are in the tool results (score)
WCHAT-69: the bare word 'safe' inside source wording or a place name is not stopped (whole-word matching and allowIn)

allowPhrases 'connectivity score': the DfT transport connectivity metric names its figure a score (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/transport-connectivity-metric/transport-connectivity-metric); quoting the metric's own name is not our score (decision 0054)

Decision 0054 and the Task 5 review: comparative verdict words (better, worse, safer, nicer, cheapest) are verdicts between areas or councils; the model-answer check excuses a negated mention such as 'neither is better or worse'

Task 5 review round 3: 'safest' and the ranking phrases 'comes first', 'comes last', 'comes out ahead' (and their forms) are verdicts or rankings (decision 0054); the model-answer check is clause by clause, so 'I won't say which comes first' passes
